definitions.explanation: Large-scale stage equipment and scenery used in theater, film, or television productions. Includes backdrops, set pieces, and structural elements. Contrasts with 小道具 (small props, hand props).

examples.japanese: {大道具|おおどうぐ}の{準備|じゅんび}が{進|すす}んでいる。
examples.english: Preparations for the stage set are underway.

examples.japanese: {大道具|おおどうぐ}を{組|く}み{立|た}てるのに{半日|はんにち}かかった。
examples.english: It took half a day to assemble the stage set.

examples.japanese: {舞台|ぶたい}{裏|うら}では{大道具|おおどうぐ}スタッフが{場面|ばめん}{転換|てんかん}のために{忙|いそが}しく{動|うご}いていた。
examples.english: Backstage, the set crew was busy moving things around for the scene change.

notes:
USAGE:
{大道具|おおどうぐ} refers to the large set pieces and scenery in theater and film. It also refers to the department or crew responsible for these items. Originally a kabuki theater term, now used broadly in all performing arts and film/TV production.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {大道具|おおどうぐ}を{組|く}む (to build the stage set)
- {大道具|おおどうぐ}スタッフ (set construction crew)
- {大道具|おおどうぐ}{担当|たんとう} (person in charge of sets)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{小道具|こどうぐ} (small props, hand props) refers to portable items used by actors on stage, such as cups, swords, or letters. Together, {大道具|おおどうぐ} and {小道具|こどうぐ} cover all physical elements of a stage production.
